features.description: Function epilogues restore several callee-saved registers with consecutive `pop` instructions, then tail-call through `jmp cs:xxx`.
Long unrolled runs repeatedly use `add reg, CONST`, often to advance a pointer or index between memory accesses and calls.

A recurring pattern is loading a pointer from the zero-offset field `[rcx]` with `mov`, then accessing or updating the value through that loaded pointer, commonly by storing a constant or a call result.
Repeatedly reload a stack-resident temporary with `mov reg, [rsp+...]` after a call, then reuse the value as a call argument or object-field value.
The code contains x86 `lock`-prefixed atomic read-modify-write instructions, often followed by a conditional jump that checks the operation’s result or flags.
Repeated `cmp` instructions feed ordered condition-code operations—especially `setnl`/`setl`, alongside relational `jcc` and `cmovcc` forms—to produce comparison booleans and direct control flow.
The code repeatedly computes element offsets or advances base pointers with `lea`, `add`/`sub`, and scaled indices, then uses them for array loads or stores inside bounds-checked loops.

Repeated table-driven logic sign-extends 16-bit values with `movsx` from scaled indexed memory operands such as `[base+index*2]`, often after widening the index with `movsxd`, then branches or performs further lookups using the result.
Repeated `cmovnz` instructions select between register values according to condition flags, often after `test al, al` or a `setp` following an unordered floating-point comparison.
Repeated short stubs set up an address or call argument and end with `jmp JUMP_ADDR_n`, converging on the same shared basic block.

An entry guard tests a value and conditionally jumps forward, leaving a short early-exit path in the fall-through and entering the main body at the branch target.

A dense decision tree repeatedly compares values with `cmp` or `test`, then uses conditional jumps such as `jz`, `jnz`, `jl`, and `jg` to route execution through shared control-flow targets.

Description: A vectorized array-processing loop uses XMM registers for packed SIMD arithmetic, with instructions such as `paddd`, `addps`, and `mulps`, vector loads and stores, and a loop-counter branch.

Switch-style dispatch on an integer selector: `cmp`-based signed and unsigned range checks (`ja`, `jbe`, `jl`, `jle`) route execution among case blocks, with jump-table forms loading a relative offset via `movsxd`, adding the table base, then using `jmp` through a register.
Functions commonly test or mask `sil`, the low byte of the second integer argument, against an immediate and use the result for a conditional branch.
Scalar floating-point code transfers 32- or 64-bit values between XMM registers and general-purpose registers or memory with `movd`/`movq`, then uses them in scalar SSE arithmetic or comparisons.

A stack-realignment prologue saves the original `rsp` in a register or stack slot, subtracts an immediate from `rsp`, masks it with `and rsp, imm`, and then establishes `rbp` from the aligned stack pointer.
The code frequently sign-extends narrow integer values into wider registers with `movsx`, often before arithmetic or indexed memory access.

A signed remainder-by-power-of-two calculation uses `cdq`/`cqo`, shifts the sign extension, adds it to the dividend, masks the result, then subtracts the sign correction.

Repeated x86 `div`/`idiv` instructions use a register divisor with the implicit `EDX:EAX` or `RDX:RAX` dividend, preceded by high-half setup such as `cdq`/`cqo` sign extension or `xor edx, edx` clearing.

The code prepares the high half of the implicit EDX:EAX or RDX:RAX dividend with `xor edx,edx`, `cdq`, or `cqo`, then performs integer `div` or `idiv` with a register or memory divisor.
Scalar floating-point code repeatedly converts double-precision values to single precision with `cvtsd2ss`, often amid `addss`/`subss` and double-precision arithmetic.
A register-level bitwise complement using `not r32` or `not r64`, with the result then used in masking, shifting, or testing logic.

The function entry saves one or more callee-saved registers with `push`, immediately allocates a stack frame with `sub rsp, CONST`, then saves an `fs:xxx` stack-canary value without setting up `rbp` as a frame pointer.

The functions repeatedly use checked contiguous-buffer growth: they derive an element span with `sub`/`sar`/`imul`, detect overflow with `cmp` and `setb` or conditional branches, then copy elements in pointer-advancing loops.
Byte-level packing and extraction using the legacy high-byte registers AH, BH, CH, or DH in `mov`/`movzx` instructions, often alongside AL and shifts or masks.
Many functions contain repeated internal `endbr64` landing pads at branch targets, often followed by register setup and an indirect `call cs:xxx`.

At CET-marked function entries, an `rbp`-based frame saves nonvolatile registers—especially `rbx`, often alongside `r12` or `r13`—before allocating local stack space.
The feature is integer division, typically a `cdq` or `cqo` sign-extension immediately followed by `idiv` on a register.

The code performs ordering and range tests by comparing operands—often a computed difference against an immediate—and using the resulting flags in condition-code instructions such as `jg`, `jl`, `jbe`, `setb`, and `setnbe`.
The code repeatedly loads pointer fields, checks them with `test reg,reg` and `jz`, then issues `prefetcht0` on the surviving pointer before continuing the traversal.
They compute a difference between size-like registers with `sub`, then compare it with immediate bounds and branch on signed conditions such as `jg`, `jl`, `jge`, and `jle`.

A large switch-style dispatcher extracts a byte-sized selector, branches through a dense run of conditional case checks, and routes cases into repeated helper-call blocks.
Near the entry, `test [rax+CONST], CONST` is followed by repeated `setnz al; movzx eax, al` boolean materialization, with the results stored in stack slots before a conditional jump.
Repeated `cmp`/`cmovcc` sequences select between register-held pointers or bounds, with the selected value then used in zero checks or boundary arithmetic.
Repeated XMM-register conversions between double- and single-precision floating point, especially `cvtsd2ss` and `cvtss2sd`, often alongside `movsd`/`movss` loads and stores.

A range-checked switch dispatch compares an index against a constant, branches with `ja` when it is out of range, then loads a signed offset from `ds:xxx`, adds a `GLOBAL_VAR` base, and jumps indirectly through the resulting register.

The functions implement length-checked buffer range copies or moves, branching on pointer overlap and zero lengths and using scalar loads and stores as fallbacks around copy-helper calls.
A recurring entry pattern is an adjacent `push rax; pop rax` pair immediately after `endbr64`, often followed by `sub rsp, CONST`.
